Cautiously neutral but with a slight negative tilt after incorporating SLOOS. The FOMC statement notes modest growth and robust employment alongside elevated inflation, but the SLOOS shows broad-based tightening in lending standards and terms across C&I, commercial real estate, residential real estate, HELOCs, auto, credit cards, and other consumer loans. Banks cite the economic outlook, higher funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity positions, collateral values, and tighter credit-scoring thresholds as reasons. Loan demand is weaker across business uses (plant/equipment, M&A, inventory, A/R), spreads have widened in CRE, loan-to-value ratios are lower, and many banks expect to tighten further—implying stronger headwinds than the statement alone suggests. Mitigants include stronger capital/liquidity at larger banks, policy backstops, and isolated easing (e.g., GSE-eligible mortgages at some mid-sized banks). Net: tighter credit transmission likely weighs on activity and hiring more than previously assumed, nudging sentiment slightly below neutral.
